intro:
A form field label, with required, invalid and disabled states.

String children are wrapped in `Label.Text` for you.
usage:
<Label isRequired>Password</Label>
<Input placeholder="Create a password" secureTextEntry />

<Label>
  <Label.Text className="text-base font-semibold">API key</Label.Text>
</Label>

parts.Text: The label text. Renders the required asterisk when the label is required.

examples.title: Marking a field required
examples.description: `isRequired` adds the asterisk and the accessibility state.

examples.title: Invalid and disabled
examples.description: Both are visual and semantic — pair them with the matching state on the field itself.
examples.code:
<Label isInvalid>Card number</Label>
<Input errorMessage="Check the number and try again." />

<Label isDisabled>Plan</Label>
<Input value="Premium" disabled />

examples.title: Custom layout
examples.description: Passing `Label.Text` instead of the `children` string is what lets the text be styled on its own — the required mark stays the label's, positioned the same way.
examples.code:
<View className="w-full gap-1.5">
  <Label isRequired>
    <Label.Text className="text-base font-semibold">API key</Label.Text>
  </Label>
  <Input placeholder="sk-…" />
</View>
